# Daily seismic noise power at broadband stations, from FDSN waveforms

`seismic_noise_power` · adapter 1.0.0 · makes `seismic_noise_power` tokens

| | |
|---|---|
| Provider | The data centre the region names (central Italy: INGV, EIDA Italia) |
| Home | https://www.fdsn.org/webservices/ |
| Licence | `CC-BY-4.0` |

## Terms

Each region names its data centre's licence (INGV's Italian networks: CC BY 4.0, cite the network DOI). Tokens carry the licence the region states.

## Cite

- INGV Seismological Data Centre (2006). Rete Sismica Nazionale (RSN). doi:10.13127/SD/X0FXNH7QFY
- MedNet Project Partner Institutions (1988). Mediterranean Very Broadband Seismographic Network (MedNet). doi:10.13127/SD/FBBBTDTD6Q
- McNamara, D. E., Buland, R. P. (2004). Ambient noise levels in the continental United States. BSSA 94, 1517-1527. doi:10.1785/012003001
- Peterson, J. (1993). Observations and modeling of seismic background noise. USGS Open-File Report 93-322.

## Access

FDSN station (text, level=channel) for coordinates and gains, then dataselect one station-month per request, 1 Hz LH channels (~14 MB a month, ~90 s from INGV), four requests in flight, cached by hash under raw/fdsn_waveforms.

## From the source to the token

| Token slot | Comes from |
|---|---|
| `kind` | `observation` |
| `lat, lon` | the station, from the station service |
| `depth_km` | (sensor depth - elevation) / 1000; elevation is above sea level |
| `time` | midnight UTC starting the day; the value covers the whole day |
| `value` | median over complete hours of mean band power, 3 bands, dB |
| `uncertainty` | 1.4826·MAD of the hours / sqrt(hours), at least 0.1 dB |
| `qualifiers` | station NET.STA, component Z/N/E, channel LOC.CHA |
| `resolution` | the station (1 m) and one day |

## Uncertainty

Derived from how much the day's hours disagree. It says how well the day's level is known, not how far the gain is off (a fixed offset per channel).

## Known issues

- One gain per channel epoch (the station service's overall sensitivity at its reference frequency): exact for flat broadband sensors in these bands; Trillium 40 s sensors read ~1 dB low at 0.05 Hz.
- A sensor swap starts a new epoch with a new gain; a level step across the swap date is the sensor, not the Earth.
- The primary and secondary bands are mostly the ocean: storms in the Mediterranean and the Atlantic move them by 10-20 dB in winter.
- Hours with any missing sample are dropped; a day with fewer than 8 hours is left out.
